subcompetencies.name: Patient Assessment and Development of a Care Plan

level_1: Efficiently gathers a focused history and physical examination to identify disease processes
Develops and prioritizes a care plan
level_2: Formulates a differential diagnosis
Continuously assesses the patient and recognizes unusual presentations
level_3: Orders and interprets imaging and laboratory evaluation
Adapts care plan for complex clinical situations
level_4: Formulates a care plan and communicates it to the team
Serves as a peer reference for unusual presentations
level_5: Integrates data into a comprehensive patient assessment
Participates in the development of clinical pathways

level_1: Responds to crisis situations as a team coordinator
level_2: Develops a differential diagnosis that includes the most likely etiologies for acute clinical deterioration
level_3: Determines the level of patient acuity to prioritize and implement an actionable care plan
level_4: Independently anticipates clinical deterioration and leads the multidisciplinary team
level_5: Triages available institutional resources to effectively resolve patient deterioration

level_1: Selects equipment, performs common intensive care unit (ICU) procedures (e.g., peripheral arterial or central venous catheterization), and recognizes complications, with guidance
Synthesizes data obtained from common and advanced ICU procedures to modify the care plan
Introduces new evidence- based ICU procedures
level_2: Interprets data obtained from common ICU procedures, with guidance
Proficiently performs common and advanced
level_3: Performs advanced ICU procedures (e.g., bronchoscopy, chest tube), with guidance
ICU procedures and troubleshoots complex complications
level_4: Interprets data obtained from advanced ICU procedures, with guidance
Proficiently synthesizes data obtained and identifies unusual findings from common and advanced ICU procedures
level_5: Performs common and advanced ICU procedures and troubleshoots common complications
Serves as a consultant for performing difficult procedures

level_1: Recognizes respiratory failure and develops a differential diagnosis and care plan, with guidance
Identifies the need for advanced intervention (e.g., extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), inhaled vasodilators) and adjunctive therapies (e.g., proning, nitric)
level_2: Selects and implements basic ventilation strategies (e.g., assist control, pressure support, non-invasive strategies)
Continuously assesses a patient and recognizes unusual presentations
level_3: Integrates relevant data to develop a patient care plan
Independently implements and adapts evidence-based ventilation strategies and advanced interventions
level_4: Selects from a variety of modes of ventilation or respiratory care techniques and initiates the appropriate interventions to optimize gas exchange and minimize complications
Serves as a consultant to respiratory care service in development of policies and procedures to optimize patient care
level_5: Identifies more complex etiologies for respiratory failure
Directs evidenced-based protocol development and refinement of ventilator strategies

subcompetencies.name: Management of Organ Dysfunction and Shock

level_1: Recognizes a patient in circulatory shock and initiates indicated therapies
Incorporates data from advanced diagnostic modalities to develop treatment plans
level_2: Initiates a basic diagnostic work-up to delineate the etiology of circulatory shock
Anticipates and acts independently to minimize the long-term consequences of circulatory shock and associated organ dysfunction
level_3: Identifies the underlying etiology for a shock state, actively manages the resuscitation, and continually assesses the response to therapy
Synthesizes data from advanced diagnostic modalities to develop a comprehensive treatment plan
level_4: Utilizes advance diagnostic modalities, with knowledge of advantages and limitations of each, to determine the etiology of shock
Is recognized by others as a resource in the management of shock and multisystem organ failure
level_5: Actively manages an unstable patient in a shock state, anticipates and acts to minimize multisystem organ dysfunction, and recognizes atypical or subtle presentations of shock
Develops diagnostic algorithms for the diagnosis and management of circulatory shock

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of the pharmacology, clinical indications, and application of medications used in the care of critically ill patients, including vasoactive drugs, sedatives, analgesics, immunotherapy, and antibiotics
level_2: Applies knowledge of the pharmacology, clinical indications, and selection of medications used in the care of critically ill patients
level_3: Applies knowledge of the pharmacology, clinical indications, and selection of medications used in the care of complex critically ill patients
level_4: Integrates knowledge of pharmacology, clinical indications, and selection of medications (including medication interactions) to care for critically ill patients
level_5: Serves as a consultant in pharmacotherapy for critically ill patients

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common pathophysiology and complications related to critical illness
level_2: Applies knowledge of common pathophysiology and complications to treat critical illness
level_3: Applies knowledge of complex pathophysiology and complications to treat critical illness
level_4: Serves as a resource for knowledge of pathophysiology and complications related to critical illness
level_5: Is recognized as an expert in synthesizing and prioritizing differential diagnosis complex critical care conditions and anticipating potential complications

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common events that impact patient safety
Describes departmental quality improvement initiatives
Discloses patient safety events to patients and patients’ families (simulated or actual)
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and patients’ families (simulated or actual)
Actively engages teams and processes to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_4: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Participates in department quality improvement initiatives
Role models or mentors others in the disclosure of patient safety events
level_5: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems (simulated or actual)
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional level or above

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination
Identifies specific population and community health needs for the local population
Role models and advocates for safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs within and across health care delivery systems
level_2: Identifies key elements for safe and effective transitions of care and hand-offs
Coordinates care of patients in complex clinical situations effectively using the roles of interprofessional team members
Participates in changing and adapting practice to provide for the needs of specific populations
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of population and community health needs
Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations
Analyzes the process of care coordination and participates in the design and implementation of improvements
level_4: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations effectively using the roles of interprofessional team members
Uses institutional resources effectively to meet the needs of a patient population and community
Improves quality of transitions of care within and across health care delivery systems to optimize patient outcomes
level_5: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in routine clinical situations
Role models effective coordination of patient- centered care among different disciplines and specialties
Advocates for populations and communities with health care needs in the peri-operative setting

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies key components of the complex health care system (e.g., hospital, skilled nursing facility, finance, personnel, technology)
Explains the impact of documentation on billing and reimbursement
level_2: States factors impacting the costs of critical care
Manages various components of the complex health care system to provide efficient and effective patient care and transition of care
level_3: Describes how components of a complex health care system are interrelated, and how this impacts patient care
Practices and advocates for cost- effective patient care
level_4: Documents patient details to facilitate accurate billing and reimbursement
Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high-value, efficient, and effective patient care
level_5: Discusses how individual practice affects the broader system (e.g., length of stay, readmission rates, clinical efficiency)
Engages in external activities related to advocacy for cost- effective care

level_1: Accesses and uses evidence in routine patient care
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and elicits patient preferences and values to guide evidence- based care
level_3: Compares and applies the best available evidence, integrated with patient preference, to the care of complex patients
level_4: Appraises and applies evidence, even in the face of uncertainty and conflicting evidence, to guide individualized care
level_5: Coaches others to appraise and apply evidence for complex patients and/or participates in the development of guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Accepts responsibility for personal and professional development by establishing goals
Designs and implements a learning plan, with prompting
Considers alternatives to improve performance
level_2: Identifies the factors that contribute to performance deficits
Seeks performance data episodically, with adaptability and humility
Integrates performance data to adapt the learning plan
level_3: Actively seeks opportunities to improve
Institutes behavioral change(s) to improve performance
Role models consistently seeking performance data with adaptability and humility
level_4: Demonstrates openness to performance data (feedback and other input) to form goals
Independently creates and implements a learning plan
Models reflective practice
level_5: Analyzes and acknowledges the factors that contribute to performance deficits
Intentionally seeks performance data consistently, with adaptability and humility
Facilitates the design and implementation of learning plans for others

level_1: Identifies potential triggers for professionalism lapses
Analyzes straightforward situations using ethical principles
Actively solicits help and acts on recommendations to resolve complex interpersonal situations
level_2: Describes when and how to report lapses in professionalism
Demonstrates professional behavior in complex or stressful situations
Recognizes and uses resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of the ethical principles underlying patient care
Recognizes need to seek help in managing and resolving complex interpersonal situations
Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations
level_4: Demonstrates insight into professional behavior in routine situations
Analyzes complex situations using ethical principles
Identifies and seeks to address system-level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution
level_5: Takes responsibility for one’s own professionalism lapses
Recognizes situations that may trigger professionalism lapses and intervenes to prevent lapses in oneself

level_1: Responds promptly to requests or reminders to complete tasks
Takes responsibility for tasks not completed in a timely manner and identifies strategies to prevent recurrence
level_2: Takes responsibility for failure to complete tasks
Prioritizes tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in complex or stressful situations
level_3: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
Proactively implements strategies to ensure that the needs of patients, teams, and systems are met
level_4: Recognizes situations that may impact one’s own ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
Designs and implements an institutional systems approach to ensure timely task completion and shared responsibility
level_5: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in routine situations

level_1: Recognizes the importance of addressing personal and professional well-being
Independently develops a plan to promote personal and professional well-being
level_2: Lists available resources for personal and professional well-being
Describes institutional factors that positively and/or negatively affect well-being
level_3: Describes institutional resources that are meant to promote/support well- being
Creates institutional-level interventions that promote colleagues’ well-being
level_4: With assistance, proposes a plan to promote personal and professional well-being
Describes institutional programs designed to examine systemic contributors to burnout
level_5: Recognizes which institutional factors affect well-being

level_1: Communicates with patients and their families in an understandable and respectful manner
Uses shared decision- making to make a personalized care plan
level_2: Provides timely updates to patients and patients’ families
Facilitates difficult discussions with patients and patients’ families
level_3: Customizes communication in the setting of biases and barriers with patients and patients’ families
Effectively negotiates and manages conflict among patients, patients’ families, and the health care team
level_4: Actively listens to patients and patients’ families to elicit patient preferences and expectations
Mentors others in the facilitation of crucial conversations
level_5: Explains complex and difficult information to patients and patients’ families
Mentors others in conflict resolution

level_1: Identifies the need to assess a patient’s/patient’s family’s expectations and understanding of health status and treatment options
Sensitively and compassionately delivers medical information; elicits a patient’s/patient’s family’s values, goals, and preferences; and acknowledges uncertainty and conflict, with guidance
level_2: Identifies key communication elements for shared decision making
Tailors communication according to disease characteristics and trajectory, patient consent, patient’s family’s needs, and medical uncertainty, and is able to address intense emotional response
level_3: Assesses a patient’s family’s/caregiver’s understanding of the patient’s condition and identifies preferences for receiving information

Independently uses shared decision making to align the patient’s/patient’s family’s values, goals, and preferences with treatment options to make a personalized care plan in situations with a high degree of uncertainty and conflict
level_4: Facilitates communication with a patient/patient’s family by introducing stakeholders, setting the agenda, clarifying expectations, and verifying an understanding of the clinical situation
Coaches others in the communication of prognostic information
level_5: Delivers difficult information and attends to emotional responses of a patient and patient’s family/caregivers
Coaches others in shared decision making in communication with a patient/patient’s family

level_1: Respectfully requests or receives consultations
Solicits feedback on performance as a member of the health care team
Maintains effective communication in crisis situations
level_2: Uses language that values all members of the health care team
Uses closed-loop communication to verify understanding
Communicates constructive feedback to superiors
level_3: Respectfully receives feedback from health care team members
Adapts communication style to fit team needs
Role models flexible communication strategies that value input from all health care team members, resolving conflict when needed
level_4: Clearly, concisely, and promptly requests or responds to a consultation
Communicates concerns and provides feedback to peers and learners
Facilitates regular health care team-based feedback in complex situations
level_5: Communicates information effectively with all health care team members
Coordinates recommendations from different members of the health care team to optimize patient care

level_1: Accurately records information in the patient record; demonstrates judicious use of documentation shortcuts
Respectfully communicates concerns about the system
Models exemplary written or verbal communication
level_2: Safeguards patient personal health information
Accurately records information in the electronic health record (EHR) and communicates complex care decisions for complex cases
Uses appropriate channels to offer clear and constructive suggestions to improve the system
level_3: Communicates through appropriate channels as required by institutional policy
Appropriately selects direct and indirect forms of communication based on context
Explores innovative uses of the EHR to facilitate effective critical care management
level_4: Accurately gathers all essential medical records from other institutions
Respectfully communicates concerns about the system and contributes to solutions
Guides departmental or institutional policies and procedures around communication
level_5: Documents required data in formats specified by institutional policy
Uses EHR functionality to highlight challenges in anesthetic care to facilitate future peri- operative management
Initiates difficult conversations with appropriate stakeholders to improve the system
